title: I've been building a multiplayer voxel world in the browser with AI for months – looking for playtesters (PixelMine, free, PC + mobile)
author: Swimming-Guarantee-7
selftext:
Hi! I'm the developer of **PixelMine** – a free browser game set in a big, snowy voxel world. No download, it runs in Chrome/Edge/Safari on PC and on phones (landscape).

**How it's made (the AI part)**

\- The code is written together with Claude (Anthropic): a custom WebGL engine (no Unity, no three.js), a Node.js server with WebSockets for multiplayer, and a lot of game systems on top. I direct, test and decide – the AI writes and fixes the code.

\- I run two AI sessions in parallel: one builds, tests and deploys the game, the other does design work (characters, HUD, menus) and hands over packages through a shared "mailbox" folder.

\- Every change goes in as a small patch script, and there are a few hundred automated browser tests plus a nightly test run before anything goes live.

\- Menu art, icons and the new mobile HUD frames are AI-generated images, cleaned up and tested in the game.

**What you can do in the game**

\- Explore an open world with villages, a snow town, a desert town, a dragon mountain, lakes, caves, sky islands and a second region in the east

\- Dig, build, farm and craft (230 block types, 240+ recipes, tool tiers, armor)

\- Talk to NPCs, follow a story and quests (it starts with Mara on the farm)

\- Day/night, weather, animals and monsters at night

\- The original core game: dig through a giant haystack to find the needle

\- Play with friends in online worlds; extra modes like Battle Royale (vs. bots or online lobbies), a 5v5 arena vs. bots, vehicles, a train and a rocket to the moon

**What I'm looking for**

Honest first impressions from people who haven't seen it before:

1. What was confusing in the first 5–10 minutes?

2. Does it feel like one coherent game or like "AI patchwork"?

3. On mobile: how do the controls feel? Anything too small or in the way?

4. Bugs, crashes, low frame rate – please add your device + browser

5. What would make you come back tomorrow?

**Good to know**

\- You need a free account (username + password) – or only username. 

\- English and German are supported.

\- The GIF/video are captured from the real game (software rendering, with camera flights); the world looks like this in-game, just not at 60 fps on that capture machine.

▶ **Play:** [https://pixelmine.online](https://pixelmine.online)

Happy to play and give feedback on your AI-made game in return – just drop a link in the comments. Thanks!

comments.author: shaymagen
comments.body: Bravo! A custom WebGL engine with no three.js, a multiplayer server, and a few hundred automated browser tests is a level of discipline you don't often see in AI-assisted builds  The world in the trailer looks great, especially the snowy town. Wishing you lots of good playtesters; you've clearly put your heart into this.

replies.author: Swimming-Guarantee-7
replies.body:
Thank you so much! I really appreciate that you took the time to look beyond just the visuals! 😊

I'm developing PixelMine as an independent project, and there's been a huge amount of work behind the scenes. AI helps me with development, but the ideas, direction and decisions are my own.

There's still a lot to improve, which is exactly why I'm looking for testers who can explore the game, find bugs and give honest feedback.

Thanks again for the encouragement! It really means a lot!
